title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-3
content:
Context:
- Intermittent throughput regression observed on prod-dedicated pool for model: redwood/open-7b-quant. Baseline QPS for 2048 seq workload ~480 QPS; since 2024-11-06 we see sustained ~320 QPS under similar traffic profiles. Latency SLOs still OK for p95 but tail has increased slightly.

Hypothesis (summary):
1) Continuous batching misconfiguration after recent autoscaler change causes suboptimal batch formation (batches smaller than optimal) leading to GPU underutilization.
2) KV cache eviction behavior changed (LRU threshold tweak) causing cache misses for long-lived chat sessions, more decoding work per request.
3) A scheduling change (nodeLabel weighting) is routing some heavy sessions to slower GPU type (A10 -> T4 fallback) during burst, reducing throughput.

Evidence / Observations:
- On 2024-11-06 03:14 UTC a commit landed that changed default continuous_batching.max_wait_ms from 12 -> 6 (PR #982).
- Metric snapshots (from console):
  - continuous_batching/avg_batch_size dropped from 7.4 -> 4.1 around 2024-11-06 03:20 UTC.
  - kv_cache/hit_rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.57 for sessions with seq>1024.
  - gpu/utilization avg down 15% for affected nodes.
- No increase in 4xx/5xx error rates. Throughput regression seems resource-efficiency related rather than request failures.

Commands tried / quick checks:
1) Check batch size timeseries (prod metrics):
  $ curl -sS "https://console.redwood-inference.internal/api/metrics?metric=continuous_batching.avg_batch_size&from=2024-11-05T00:00Z&to=2024-11-07T00:00Z&step=1h" | jq .
  -> confirmed drop coincident with deploy.

2) Query running config on serving nodes (example):
  $ kubectl -n serving get configmap continuous-batching -o yaml | grep -A3 max_wait_ms
  max_wait_ms: "6"
  min_batch_size: "2"
  max_batch_size: "16"

3) Reproduce locally with loadtest (mini-cluster):
  - start a) 4 workers with identical model and seq=2048 load generator (rps target 600)
  - with max_wait_ms=6 -> observed avg batch size ~3.9, qps ~320
  - with max_wait_ms=12 -> avg batch size ~7.2, qps ~515

4) Inspect KV cache logs for eviction spikes:
  $ kubectl logs -n serving pod/kv-cache-0 | grep -i eviction | tail -n 50
  [2024-11-06T03:19:12Z] INFO eviction: evicted 34 entries, threshold 0.75
  [2024-11-06T03:22:05Z] INFO eviction: evicted 58 entries, threshold 0.75

5) Check node GPU types and recent scheduling events:
  $ kubectl get pods -o wide -n serving | grep redwood-open-7b
  -> some pods scheduled to node-type=t4-fallback around 03:25 UTC when cluster was scaling.

Error snippets / logs:
- Worker log (serving-runtime) when batch formation smaller:
  WARN 2024-11-06T03:21:04.123Z batching: small batch (size=2) after wait_ms=6 for model redwood/open-7b-quant
  DEBUG 2024-11-06T03:21:04.125Z kvcache: miss for session s-83f... key len=1536

- Autoscaler / scheduling log:
  INFO 2024-11-06T03:24:01Z autoscaler: scaled up 3 nodes type=t4-fallback due to ephemeral spike

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Rolled back continuous_batching.max_wait_ms to 12 in a subset of nodes (canary): avg_batch_size recovered to ~7 and qps recovered by ~50% on canary nodes.
- Toggled kv-cache LRU threshold back to previous value for canary -> hit_rate improved ~10%
- Pinned critical serving pods to A10 pool with nodeSelector for a small subset (recovery observed).

Notes on configs to investigate further:
- continuous_batching.min_batch_size = 2 (maybe too low for our seq distribution). Consider bump to 3 or 4 for model with seq>1024.
- max_wait_ms tradeoff: lower reduces latency for sparse traffic but hurts throughput for bursty medium-load. We need adaptive policy (longer wait for high seq workloads).
- autoscaler policy: ensure type-preference for critical model families; avoid T4 fallback unless absolutely needed.

Hypotheses to validate / experiments:
- H1: Increasing max_wait_ms to 14 during sustained traffic will restore throughput with acceptable p95 latency (run A/B for 4h).
- H2: Enforce min_batch_size=4 for seq>1024 sessions will increase GPU utilization and throughput without increasing tail latency beyond 5%.
- H3: KV cache eviction tuning (increase mem cap by 25%) will restore hit rate and reduce per-request decode workload by ~12%.

Planned experiments (next 48h):
1) Canary rollout: change max_wait_ms=14 on 10% of capacity for redwood/open-7b-quant. Monitor avg_batch_size, QPS, p95 latency, kv_cache hit_rate for 2 hours. (Owner: Alex)
2) Launch load test for min_batch_size=4 vs 2 on staging with realistic session distribution (seq histogram from last week). (Owner: Michael)
3) Increase kv-cache capacity by 25% on canary and measure hit rate delta. (Owner: Priya)
4) Lock scheduling weights to prefer A10 for top-traffic models during top-traffic windows for next 24 hours. (Owner: Infra oncall)

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- What prompted the max_wait_ms change in PR #982? Was this an optimization for latency on small seq workloads? Need design rationale from author. (Action: ask PR author in slack)
- Is there automated regression alerting for avg_batch_size drops? If not, add an alert (threshold: drop >25% over 30m).
- Check cost impact if we keep higher max_wait_ms: might increase tail latency but reduces token cost by improving batch efficiency. Need cost-vs-latency analysis.

Quick links / references:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-1247 (throughput regression incident)
- Perf dashboard: https://console.redwood-inference.internal/dashboards/serving/batching

Notes to self (scratchy):
- reproduces locally -> big indicator config change not model change.
- kv-cache hit drop suggests eviction + smaller batches = double hit to perf.
- schedule + autoscaler made it worse by routing to weaker GPUs.

If experiments show positive, create a small RFC: "adaptive-continuous-batching-policy" with rules: bump max_wait_ms for long-seq workloads, min_batch_size adaptive, and autoscaler node-type preference mapping.

End of scratchpad.
